rationale: BullMQ is a mature, production-grade Redis-based job queue with 104 TypeScript source files (23.5K lines), 115 atomic Lua command scripts, and 58 test files. It provides all queue primitives needed for a scraping pipeline: job scheduling with cron/interval repeat strategies, parent-child flow dependencies for multi-step scrapes, priority queues, rate limiting (global and per-group), delayed jobs with exponential backoff, deduplication (debounce/throttle), stalled job recovery, job cancellation with abort signals, sandboxed workers for isolation, and OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry. The architecture uses a clean backend abstraction (IQueueBackend) supporting both Redis and PostgreSQL. It is multi-language (Node, Python, Elixir, Rust, PHP, .NET). Directly addresses the 'queue' pipeline concern with S-tier depth and relevance.
limitations: Requires Redis (or PostgreSQL) as external dependency
BullMQ-Pro features (groups, batches, observables) are closed-source
Lua script complexity may require Redis expertise for debugging
Cluster mode requires Redis Cluster with specific key-slot patterns
